title: loopctl runs in lax and den, with every machine kept running

story.as_a: session on any machine of the fleet
story.i_want_to: reach a running loopctl machine in two Fly regions, none of them ever suspended
story.so_that: a lost machine or host in one region never takes loopctl away, and the real-time subscriptions R11 holds stay up

rationale: PRD R9: loopctl runs in lax plus Fly den, and each region keeps at least one machine that is never suspended. fly.toml cannot give that today: min_machines_running = 2 (fly.toml:180) binds only in primary_region = "lax" (fly.toml:5), and auto_stop_machines = "suspend" (fly.toml:176) would suspend a den machine. EXPECTED_APP_NODES = "2" (fly.toml:171) is the machine count Loopctl.DbCapacity multiplies the pools by and Loopctl.ClusterReadiness alarms against, so it must rise with the machine count. A region's machine count is not expressible in fly.toml at all, so it needs one checked-in list and a deploy step that holds it.

acceptance_criteria.description: fly.toml [http_service] sets auto_stop_machines = "off" (was "suspend"), so no machine in any region is ever stopped or suspended by the proxy; auto_start_machines stays true.
deploy/regions.txt lists one line per region, "<region> <machines>", holding "lax 2" and "den 1"; fly.toml's EXPECTED_APP_NODES equals the sum of its counts ("3").

DbCapacity.fits?(DbCapacity.verified_live_max_connections(), n) is true for n = fly.toml's EXPECTED_APP_NODES, with @verified_live_max_connections and @verified_on re-measured against ecf-postgres (the database loopctl moved to) at release time.

deploy/ensure-regions.sh reads deploy/regions.txt and, for each region whose app process group has fewer machines than its count, runs `flyctl scale count <count> --region <region> --process-group app --yes -a loopctl`; a region already at or above its count gets no scale call.
After scaling, deploy/ensure-regions.sh exits 1 with a line `region <r>: <k> started machines, need <n>` for every region whose started machines are fewer than its count, and exits 0 otherwise.
The ci.yml deploy job runs `bash deploy/ensure-regions.sh` as the step after `flyctl deploy --remote-only`, so a failed region check fails the deploy job before the post-deploy smoke.
GET /health answers with a `region` field holding the FLY_REGION the answering machine runs in, or null off Fly; the status code still depends on database and Oban only.

test_cases.name: fly.toml keeps every machine running and EXPECTED_APP_NODES matches the region list (unit, fly_toml_test)
preconditions: fly.toml and deploy/regions.txt read with the file's existing section/2 and env_table/1 helpers
steps: sum the counts in deploy/regions.txt and compare with [env] EXPECTED_APP_NODES
expected_results: auto_stop_machines is off; the sum equals EXPECTED_APP_NODES; the existing CLUSTER_PEERS_MAY_SUSPEND test still passes with the variable unset

test_cases.name: the connection budget fits at the deployed node count (unit, db_capacity_test)
preconditions: EXPECTED_APP_NODES parsed from fly.toml with DbCapacity.parse_expected_app_nodes/1
expected_results: true; verified_on is on or after the release-10 branch cut

test_cases.name: ensure-regions scales only the short region (unit, stub flyctl)
preconditions: a temp dir on PATH holding a stub flyctl that answers `machines list --json` with two lax app machines and none in den, and appends every other argv to a log file
steps: System.cmd("bash", ["deploy/ensure-regions.sh"]) with the stub first on PATH
run it again with the stub now listing one started den machine
expected_results: the first run logs exactly one `scale count 1 --region den` call; the second run logs no scale call

test_cases.name: ensure-regions fails naming the region that did not start (unit, stub flyctl)
preconditions: a stub flyctl whose den machine stays in state `stopped` after the scale call
expected_results: exit status 1; output contains `region den: 0 started machines, need 1`

test_cases.name: the deploy job checks regions right after the deploy (unit)
steps: read jobs.deploy.steps and find the index of the `flyctl deploy --remote-only` step
expected_results: the next step's run is `bash deploy/ensure-regions.sh`

test_cases.name: /health names the region, null off Fly (ConnCase)
preconditions: no FLY_REGION in the test environment; the default health checker stub
steps: the pure region reader on %{"FLY_REGION" => "den"} and on %{}
expected_results: 200 with "region": null; the reader gives "den" and nil

technical_notes: fly.toml: primary_region :5, the [env] clustering comment :158-169 and EXPECTED_APP_NODES :171, [http_service] auto_stop_machines :176, auto_start_machines :177, min_machines_running :180 (keep it, with its comment changed to say it binds lax only and auto_stop off is what keeps den running). Rewrite the :163-169 comment for three machines in two regions.

test/loopctl/fly_toml_test.exs: section/2 :102, env_table/1 :85, the clustering describe :118-146. The CLUSTER_PEERS_MAY_SUSPEND test (:132) computes may_suspend? from auto_stop and min_running, so with auto_stop off it requires the variable to stay unset; no change to that test.

Loopctl.DbCapacity: @verified_live_max_connections 100 and @verified_on 2026-06-24 (lib/loopctl/db_capacity.ex:87-90) were measured on fly mpg; loopctl's database has since moved to ecf-postgres, whose max_connections is 300 shared by six databases, with per-role CONNECTION LIMITs (loopctl 80, rls_user 60; infra runbooks/postgres-monitoring.md:357-363). Re-measure the binding limit for loopctl's two roles and record it with its date. peak_total/2 (:294) at 3 nodes with the prod pools (:43) is 89; at 4 it is 111, so a second den machine needs a pool change first.

Clustering needs no change: DNS_CLUSTER_QUERY = loopctl.internal (fly.toml:170) resolves every started machine in every region over 6PN, and ClusterReadiness.readiness/0 (lib/loopctl/cluster_readiness.ex:153) reports :clustered at expected 3 once two peers are connected.

ci.yml: the deploy job is at .github/workflows/ci.yml:1655, its deploy step runs `flyctl deploy --remote-only` at :1669, and the post-deploy smoke job follows at :1673. ensure-regions.sh uses the same FLY_API_TOKEN the deploy step has; it reads regions.txt and machine state from `flyctl machines list --json -a loopctl` (fields region, state, config.metadata.fly_process_group).

/health: LoopctlWeb.HealthController.check/2 (lib/loopctl_web/controllers/health_controller.ex:49) json-encodes the checker's map; add region there, read through one pure function over an env map so the test needs no System.put_env (CLAUDE.md Test Conventions rule 2). The pattern is Loopctl.Runners.machine_id/0 (lib/loopctl/runners.ex:1555). Version stays undisclosed (#461 item 5, health_controller.ex:6). FLY_REGION gets a row in deploy/FLY_SECRETS.md beside FLY_MACHINE_ID (:72), and the EXPECTED_APP_NODES row (:88) changes its default text to the fly.toml value (mix loopctl.check_env_docs).

The database stays single-primary in lax (PRD R9): a den machine reaches ecf-postgres over 6PN across regions, so every query from den pays the lax-den round trip. That cost is measured in the definition of done, not designed away here.
non_goals: A read replica or a database in den: after the first incident (PRD R9).
Probing each region from outside: US-52.63, which reads the region field this story adds.
Restoring the database in den: US-52.63's drill and runbook.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.60.1: a partition that cuts one region off leaves the other region's machines running and serving, because none of them is ever suspended waiting for traffic to wake it.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.60.2: the per-region machine count lives in one checked-in file that the deploy reads and fly_toml_test binds to EXPECTED_APP_NODES, so the count cannot live only in Fly's machine list.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.60.4: ensure-regions scales only a region below its count, so a re-run deploy job adds no machine.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.60.5: a machine that is slow to start fails the deploy job with the region named, instead of the deploy reporting success with a region empty.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.60.7: /health names the machine's region, so a probe that asked for a region can tell whether that region answered.

definition_of_done: After the deploy: `flyctl machines list -a loopctl --json` shows two started app machines in lax and one in den, and none suspended after an hour with no traffic.
Loopctl.ClusterReadiness.readiness() on any machine (fly ssh console, bin/loopctl rpc) returns status :clustered with expected_nodes 3.
p50 and p95 of GET /api/v1/projects answered in den and in lax over 50 requests each are written into the PR body, as the measured cost of a den machine reaching the lax database.
defaults: Machines per region: lax 2, den 1 (owner may change; a fourth machine needs a pool-size change first, technical_notes).
auto_stop_machines = "off" for every region, rather than a per-region setting Fly does not offer.
